dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth by about a factor of two between sectors and even between different pipelines, and individual dips disagree strongly. There is also a strong secondary dip at about one third depth in the same orbit. The transit lasts longer than expected for the small M dwarf. Together this looks like a stellar eclipsing binary / blended binary signal, not a 3.6 Earth-radius planet on target, and centroiding could not confirm it is even on the target.

reasons.why: Strong second dip near phase 0.677 with ~37% of primary depth, well above brightenings and not at 0.5, matches stellar companion eclipse; beat_brightening argument is compensated but SNR>5 favors binary.
reasons.value: snr 5.789, depth_ppm 4964, depth_over_dip 0.3684, phase 0.677, best_brightening_snr 4.015, secondary_over_bump 1.442

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor ~2 between sectors and between pipelines, opposite to expectation for a planet. sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source, so not a calibration offset.
reasons.value: 0.0006819, depth_change_pct 70, SPOC 11864+/-1249 ppm vs QLP 24640+/-3548 ppm, sector_depths_by_source changes_within_a_source

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent; signal is not reproducible with orbit, favors few scattered events or binary with spot/systematic changes over a repeatable planet transit.

Duration much longer than central for a 0.281 Rsun M dwarf (RATIO up to 1.5 allowed), indicating low stellar density inferred from transit does not match star; favours blended/stellar EB geometry over planet transit.
No difference image to confirm on-target; with off-target alternative allowed, positive secondary and variable depth support blend/EB rather than planet on target.
Machine scorer ranks as highly planet-unlike (median planet 0.5, only one planet in ten this low), consistent with secondary, depth change and duration mismatch.
